notes_for_parent: V2 is the only case pinning a SAME-BYTE-COUNT vault tamper; V3 pins the source-side counterpart, V4 vault-absent, V5 source-absent — together they isolate each conjunct of the ledger match.
The primary tamper's byte-count equality (215/215) is deliberate: any tool that shortcuts on size or mtime will report VERIFIED and be caught.

Do not change the payload bytes without updating SHA_* constants in make-fixture.sh, the selftest constants, and expected.template.json (--print-hashes prints the table; the builder asserts the constants at build time).

The case-dir expected.json stays in placeholder form (identical to expected.template.json); only the built root receives the substituted copy, so the committed copy never points at a reaped temp root. Runner-28 builds its own root under mktemp and reads <ROOT>/expected.json.
